component.name: rttx
component.summary: A tiling terminal emulator for GNOME

description.p: rttx is a tiling terminal emulator built with GTK4 and Libadwaita, organized around named workspaces and split panes. The rttx-server daemon owns each workspace's pane tree and durable state, so persistent workspaces, per-pane shell history, and the visible screen survive detach, reconnect, and daemon restart. It also features input synchronization, saved places and reusable command snippets, and drag-and-drop layout rearrangement.

screenshot.caption: rttx with split panes and workspace sidebar

description.p: Fixes panes coming back broken after a reconnect or a daemon restart: the daemon now keeps a cell grid per pane and hands an attaching client a clean rendering of the pane's state, so lines are intact, the cursor is where the shell left it, a dead app's modes and scroll region are cleared, and a prompt is never drawn over old history. Fixes "Reconnect" on one workspace silently disconnecting every other workspace on the same host, and lets the client that lost a workspace to a take-over take it back. The daemon now owns workspace names: it derives them from the shell's directory, records user renames, and keeps every window in agreement.

Adds next-pane and previous-pane shortcuts that keep a pane zoomed, a header-bar quick toggle for the terminal theme, and taking over a workspace already connected on another client. Fixes an intermittent startup crash caused by a use-after-free in GTK's Wayland input method, distinct light and dark terminal palettes, and workspace-rename persistence across restarts.
Adds a Support link in the About window and a donation URL for software centers, ships the reworked Fedora source package, and fixes terminal-mode reset after a daemon restart.
First stable release: server-authoritative workspaces with durable pane identity and crash-safe per-pane shell history, plus a clean 1.0 baseline with all pre-release migration code removed.
This release adds disconnect visualization for persistent panes, remote daemon lifecycle management, and force retry for stuck connections.
